images.title: Ends and centre of two groups
images.purpose: Show the boys' and girls' heights as two range strips on one scale with each group's mean, so students see girls are taller on the whole yet the ranges overlap.
images.composition: Two horizontal strips, Boys above Girls, on one shared light scale, each with a mean tick; wide margins around them.
exact_structure: A light grey (#6B7280) scale line from 125 to 160 cm with small unnumbered ticks every 5 runs under both strips.
Upper strip, labelled Boys at its left: a teal (#0072B2) horizontal bar from 128 to 158, with its end values 128 and 158 printed at its two ends.
Lower strip, labelled Girls at its left: an amber (#E69F00) horizontal bar from 136 to 156, with its end values 136 and 156 printed at its two ends.
On each bar a reddish purple (#CC79A7) vertical tick marks the mean: at 142.9 on the boys' bar, labelled Mean ≈ 142.9 above it, and at 146.9 on the girls' bar, labelled Mean ≈ 146.9 below it.
The girls' bar lies wholly inside the stretch of the boys' bar, showing the overlap.
rejection: a boys' bar that does not run from 128 to 158
a girls' bar that does not run from 136 to 156
the girls' mean tick drawn left of the boys' mean tick
the bars drawn on different scales
images.takeaway: Girls are taller on average, but the tallest and shortest students are boys, so not every girl is taller.
images.description: Two range bars on one scale: boys from 128 to 158 cm with mean about 142.9, girls from 136 to 156 cm with mean about 146.9.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Read the ends first, then the mean ticks, and ask whether every girl is taller than every boy.

image_decisions.why: Comparing two groups needs the extremes and the centre side by side, which the range strips show cleanly.
